API reference - generated from the OpenAPI document

  1. Overview
  2. API reference

Every network API used by the ChomikBox 2.0.8.2 Windows client of chomikuj.pl: the WCF SOAP service, upload/resume/download HTTP endpoints, web auto-login URLs, crash reporter and updater.

Every page in this section is generated from the OpenAPI 3.2.1 document by site/tools/build-api.mjs. Each operation page shows the method and URL, the SOAPAction, the request and response schemas as XML element trees, every captured example, the differences between the client's expected behaviour and the live service, and the verification status. Background on how the protocol works is on Protocol and Flows.

The project publishes two content-equivalent OpenAPI 3.2.1 documents, generated from the same source. api/chomikbox.openapi.yaml is the strictly conformant canonical document: SOAP is a single POST on /services/ChomikBoxService.svc with a SOAPAction enum and oneOf request and response bodies. api/chomikbox.per-operation.openapi.yaml is a per-operation view with one path item per SOAP operation, routed through a ?op= server URL; because a server URL may not contain a query, it declares that deviation in x-oas-deviation. The site's API reference is generated from api/chomikbox.per-operation.openapi.json.

Client API - Everything ChomikBox 2.0.8.2 calls

Operations the desktop client performs: the SOAP service plus the upload, resume and file-download HTTP endpoints.

Session model - x-session

OpenAPI security schemes cannot express a token inside the SOAP body, so the document describes the session in the extension x-session:

transport
SOAP body: <token> is the first child of every request except Auth and SessionBegin. No cookies, no HTTP auth, no SOAP header.
issuedBy
auth (AuthResult/token, with hamsterId and name)
invalidatedBy
logout (only the token it carries)
badTokenHandling
status=BadToken -> the client re-runs Auth (message-relog-count = 1 per message), replaces <token> in queued messages and resends them; messages flagged sessionBound are dropped. Messages flagged noRetransmit (Logout, CheckEvents) or noRelog (BoxEvents) are not retried.
concurrency
Multiple tokens of one account are valid concurrently; a new Auth does not invalidate earlier tokens (verified live).
lifetime
No expiry observed within ~45 minutes (not measured beyond).
timers
CheckEvents: one single-shot timer whose period is the shortest one currently requested: 300 s normally, 60 s while uploading, 15 s while a folder view is open (default values). Folders refresh every 300 s; SOAP reply timeout connection-timeout 20 s (clamped 5..120); pending-message validator every 5 s aborts messages older than 15 s (Download 45 s).
webSession
LoginFromBox?t=<token> converts the SOAP token into a web session cookie (ChomikSession).

Security considerations - from the spec

Summary of the security, privacy and robustness register; the full discussion is on the site page [Security](../site/security.html). Ratings are a coarse guide for readers of this documentation, not a formal assessment (High = exposes credentials or account control; Medium = exposes private data or can silently damage data; Low = information disclosure or hardening gap; Info = behaviour worth knowing). Affected operations carry the relevant entries in x-security-notes.

IDRatingFinding
C-01HighAll client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it.
C-02HighThe login credential passHash is an unsalted MD5 of the password, sent in clear in every Auth: it is password-equivalent and cheap to crack.
C-03MediumThe same hash is stored in conf.ini ([userinfo] password-hash, plus proxy credentials), readable by any process running as the user.
C-04HighCrash reports upload conf.ini (with the password hash), message.log, both transfer queues, the playlist, chomikId and chomikName over plain HTTP to bts.box.chomikuj.pl:8088; the only integrity value is MD5 of project-version.arch.
C-05LowVerbose logging by default (message.log), which then rides along in crash reports.
C-06MediumThe session token travels in clear in every SOAP body and as a URL query parameter (LoginFromBox?t=), where it becomes a full web session (ChomikSession) and can leak via logs, history and proxies.
C-07High (requires a network position)Updates come over plain HTTP and are applied with administrator rights, protected only by an unauthenticated hash: each package is checked by SHA-1 against the sha1 attribute of packages.xml, which comes over the same channel without any verification (no signature, no key; a mismatch is called "Signature error"), and installer.exe runs package commands without any prior check. Anyone who can alter the traffic (hostile network, DNS, proxy) can supply a matching manifest and package that runs elevated. The repository answered 404/403 on 2026-10-24, but a network attacker does not need the real server.
C-08LowThe single-instance named pipe and the chomik:// scheme accept commands (-d<url>, -u, -p) from any local process or web link. The pipe also accepts --file-server <host>, which redirects all uploads and resume checks, upload keys included, to that host (command Observed; effect Inferred, the link to the upload path was not fully confirmed).
C-09InfoUsage data stats{isUploading, isPlaying, isDownloading, panelSelectedTab, animation} rides on every CheckEvents poll. BoxEvents is not off by default: it sends fixed events whenever they occur (shutdown = poweroff/suspend/quit, detected.defaultplayer, settings.defaultplayer, settings.autostart).
C-10Infobase.ini key and similar checks are integrity/tamper detection, not authentication.
C-11InfoInternal addresses are hard-coded in client components (e.g. RFC1918 192.168.10.30 in chomikbox1conf.exe).
C-12InfoThe NPAPI "Click Catcher" browser plug-in is obsolete; modern browsers no longer load it.
S-01MediumAccount enumeration via Auth: an unknown user gets Forbidden, a known user with a wrong password gets PermissionError.
S-02MediumFolder passwords are returned in plain text over HTTP: ModifyFolder echoes the new password, Folders lists each folder's password, and the folder created by SavePlaylist gets a server-generated password while passwd=false.
S-03Medium (integrity)A fault that does not roll back: MoveFolder with newFolderId = folderId returns a:InternalServiceFault (HTTP 500), but the folder has still been moved to the account root.
S-04Medium (data loss)RemoveFolder force=false only protects folders that contain files; a folder holding only subfolders is deleted with all of them, status Ok.
S-05Low-MediumSilent fallbacks instead of errors: Folders with an unknown folderId returns the root; MoveFolder to an unknown parent moves the folder to the root (Ok); UploadToken with an unknown folderId returns Ok.
S-06LowOut-of-order or wrong-namespace parameters are silently dropped (null/0); some malformed requests (operation element without the trailing slash, the hamsterId/folderId Download id, an empty Auth) trigger an unhandled a:InternalServiceFault. The client's own "download folder" action builds exactly that hamsterId/folderId id, so that feature presumably fails against today's server (Inferred).
S-07LowContract disclosure through faults and headers: a:DeserializationFailed names parameters and CLR types, a:DestinationUnreachable leaks internal origin host names, and responses carry x-powered-by: ASP.NET and x-server.
S-08LowSigned File.aspx?e=…&pv=… download URLs are reusable bearer URLs (repeat GET and Range work); expire was always empty, so their lifetime is unknown.
S-09InfoImage.aspx?id=<fileId> redirects anonymously to a signed URL (observed for an own PNG in a non-protected folder; file ids are sequential; protected folders untested).
S-10InfoConcurrent sessions are allowed; Logout invalidates only its own token; no expiry was observed within about 45 minutes.
S-11InfoThe client identity is not enforced: Auth accepts any ver and works without the client element, so any program can present itself as ChomikBox.
S-12Lowsession.box.chomikuj.pl (SessionBegin) no longer resolves in DNS; whoever registered it would receive the user name and password hash from old clients with session-enabled=true (off by default).
S-13Low (correctness)Sequenced-Download state is per session, not per request: stored parts are keyed by the session token (not the stamp), are not cleared by a final part, and a stale part from another folder makes a later final part silently return an empty list (status Ok). Clients that reuse a session can get wrong or empty results.
S-14InfoModifyFolder accepts description, freePoints and freeTransfer and silently ignores them: any in-range value (including -1, Int32.MaxValue and a 10,000-character description) returns Ok and moves modifyTime, but nothing is echoed, Folders never returns a value, and no effect was visible in download offers, public pages or the balance. The client never sends these fields.

The full findings register, with ratings and evidence, is on Security & privacy.

About this document

Unofficial description of every network API used by ChomikBox 2.0.8.2 (Windows desktop client of chomikuj.pl, Qt 4, released 2017-10-21), documented from the client's behaviour and verified against the production service on 2026-10-24. Open questions were then settled by a live follow-up on 2026-10-24/25. Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the live behaviour is documented and the difference is recorded in x-discrepancies.

> Non-conformance notice: per-operation view. This document intentionally deviates from OAS 3.2.1 §4.5.1 (Server Object url: "Query and fragment MUST NOT be part of this URL"). Each SOAP operation gets its own path item (/Auth, /Folders, …) by declaring the path-level server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so the concatenated URL becomes …/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Auth. The physical endpoint (POST http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc) and the dispatch by SOAPAction are identical to the canonical document; WCF ignores the query. Tools that parse the server URL instead of concatenating strings may build …svc/Auth?op=, which fails. The deviation is declared in x-oas-deviation. **The strictly conformant document chomikbox.openapi.yaml (one post on the physical endpoint, SOAPAction enum, oneOf envelopes, x-soap-operations) is canonical**; it is generated from this file by tools/build-strict.mjs.

Status and disclaimer

Unofficial documentation, not affiliated with or endorsed by chomikuj.pl or the ChomikBox authors. It grants no rights to the described service and no licence to its content (info.license is a LicenseRef stating exactly that). Test only against your own account and inside a dedicated sandbox folder: some server behaviours are destructive (see Security considerations S-03, S-04, S-05).

SOAP in OpenAPI: conventions of this per-operation view

One path item per SOAP operation. WCF dispatches on the SOAPAction header and ignores the query string, while a path suffix (.svc/Auth) fails with a:DestinationUnreachable and .svc;Auth-style matrix parameters redirect (302). Each operation therefore has its own path key (/Auth, /Folders, …) and a path-item-level server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, giving …/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Auth (verified live: status Ok). This is the declared deviation above; the canonical document models the same operations as one post on the physical endpoint.

Every SOAP operation here is a post with a required SOAPAction header whose schema is const http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/<Op> (sent unquoted), media type text/xml, and the extensions x-soap-action, x-verification, x-session, x-evidence and, where relevant, x-security-notes and x-discrepancies.

SOAP wire format

Requests: POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8, always UTF-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/<Op> (unquoted). Body: <s:Envelope xmlns:s="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" s:encodingStyle="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/"><s:Body><Op xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…, no SOAP header, no indentation, children unprefixed. Parameter order matters: WCF's DataContractSerializer reads forward only and silently drops an out-of-order parameter. Booleans: the client writes 0/1, true/false work too. Request bodies may be gzip-compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip; the client does this). Service-level outcomes (including BadToken and Error) come with HTTP 200 and a status member; HTTP 500 carries a WCF SOAP fault.

Default HTTP headers of the client. ChomikBox itself sets only Content-Type, SOAPAction and Content-Encoding: gzip on SOAP requests. Qt 4.8.5 adds its defaults to every QNetworkAccessManager request that does not set them: User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (no product or version token), Accept-Encoding: gzip (replies are gunzipped transparently), Accept-Language: <locale>,en,* from the Windows locale (e.g. pl-PL,en,*; en,* for the C locale, <name>,* for en-* locales), Connection: Keep-Alive and Host (Observed for the Qt library, Inferred with high confidence for the client, which sets none of these itself). The SOAP captures send the same set (with Accept-Language: en,*). Exceptions: the music player's stream GET sends Accept-Encoding: (a single space) to switch gzip off, and uploads over the default raw-socket transport ([proto-box] direct-upload=true) bypass the Qt HTTP stack, so these defaults presumably do not apply there (Inferred). crashsender.exe and the updater use the same Qt library (Inferred: same defaults).

Namespaces. All request members are in http://chomikuj.pl/ (with trailing slash). Responses: <OpResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><OpResult xmlns:a="http://chomikuj.pl" xmlns:i="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><a:status>…; nested struct members (FolderInfo, FileEntry, settings, …) are unprefixed, i.e. in http://chomikuj.pl/. CheckEventsResult and AddFolderResult differ: a: is http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox, status/errorMessage redeclare xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl", and changes children use b: = …/TeamSolutions.Chomik.Library.DAO.ChomikBox. The real client matches by local name only.

XML modelling. Schemas use the OAS 3.2 XML Object on every element: xml.namespace is always explicit (absent means "no namespace", as for SOAP fault children), xml.prefix records the prefix used on the wire (absent means unprefixed). Reusable content components (FolderInfo, Token, …) carry xml.nodeType: none, and the element name/namespace/prefix is declared at the point of use next to the $ref (OAS 3.2 §4.26.6.6 pattern). Lists are type: array with xml.nodeType: element (wrapper) and named items. i:nil="true" maps to null (nullable types). Attributes (<resp res="1" fileid="…"/>, xml:lang) use nodeType: attribute; mixed element+text uses nodeType: text. Property order equals wire order.

Session model

There is no HTTP-level authentication. Auth returns a token, which the client sends as the first child <token> of every other SOAP request body (not expressible as an OpenAPI security scheme; see x-session and the Token schema). status=BadToken means the token is unknown or logged out; the client then re-runs Auth once and resends the message. Several tokens of one account are valid at the same time; Logout ends only its own token; no expiry was seen within ~45 minutes. The same token is passed as t= to the web auto-login URL (security scheme boxToken).

Examples

Every captured case in api/examples/<Dir>/<case>.* appears as a named Example Object: 142 cases from the first live run and 85 from the follow-up of 2026-10-24/25, whose descriptions name the follow-up run. serializedValue holds the captured bytes after redaction and, where noted, elision (Folders/root-depth2 has pre-existing folders elided and an XML comment inserted; see each example's description), or the body part of raw .http captures; dataValue holds the same data as parsed against the schema. The file is referenced with the extension **x-externalValue**, not externalValue: OAS 3.2.1 (§4.19.1) and its JSON Schema forbid serializedValue and externalValue in the same Example Object. x-externalValue-part: body marks a value that is the body of a raw HTTP capture; x-capture-meta points to the capture metadata (headers, sizes, timing, notes). Captures that have no body to show (GET requests, redirect responses) are kept as whole HTTP messages under x-request-examples (operation) and x-response-examples (response). Examples without a capture are labelled "Derived from client behaviour (not captured live)".

Captures are redacted with these placeholders: {{COOKIE}}, {{EXISTING_FOLDER_NAME}}, {{FOLDER_PASSWORD}}, {{OTHER_PATH}}, {{OTHER_USER}}, {{PASS_HASH}}, {{RANDOM_PASS_HASH}}, {{SEED}}, {{SESSION_ID}}, {{SIGNED_E}}, {{SIGNED_PV}}, {{SIGNED_URL}}, {{STAMP}}, {{TOKEN}}, {{UPLOAD_TOKEN}}, {{USERNAME}}, {{WRONG_PASS_HASH}}. NOT-A-REAL-TOKEN is a deliberately fake token. sandbox-pass-123 (ModifyFolder examples) is a throw-away password the capture tool set on its own, since-deleted sandbox folder; it is not a secret. {{OTHER_USER}}/{{OTHER_PATH}} replace other users' account names and paths in the read-only foreign-file Download captures (file extensions kept). Numeric account/folder/file ids are real. The Content-Length values in raw captures refer to the unredacted bytes.

Verification status

x-verification on every operation (also as badge tags): verified-live = request and response shapes confirmed against production; partially-verified = some parts not exercised live (named in the operation description); unverified = documented from the client's behaviour only, never exercised against the service. The badge probe marks operations the client never sends (live probes of unused URLs and of the endpoint's failure modes). x-evidence lists the example files behind each operation (paths relative to this file).

Current status (38 operations): 33 verified-live (23 client-facing + 10 probes), 5 unverified.

  • probes (badge probe, never sent by the client): getSettings (a service operation the client never calls), probeSessionPath, headFile, imageRedirect, musicFileLegacy, openPublicFolderPage, openPublicFilePage, loginFromBoxLegacy, soapRestStylePath, getServiceMetadataPage
  • unverified: sessionBegin, sendCrashReport, getUpdateRepository, getUpdatesDirectory, openBetaRepository

Servers - hosts in the document

  • http://box.chomikuj.pl: Main service host (behind Cloudflare). Paths below that live elsewhere declare their own servers.
  • http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=: ChomikBoxService WCF endpoint; the trailing ?op= turns the path key into an ignored query (…svc?op=/Auth).
  • http://{sessionHost}: Session server as configured in the client: [proto-webox] webservice-session, default session.box. + base.ini domain. session.box.chomikuj.pl has no DNS record.
  • http://{uploadServer}: Upload server returned by UploadToken (server, host:port, varies per ticket; not behind Cloudflare, Microsoft-HTTPAPI/2.0).
  • http://{fileServer}: File server named in the signed URL (sNNNN.chomikuj.pl, IIS 10, not behind Cloudflare).
  • http://chomikuj.pl: Working host (verified live).
  • http://www.chomikuj.pl: Host built by the client.
  • http://music.chomikuj.pl: Host in the template (unreachable).
  • http://bts.box.chomikuj.pl:8088: Crash collector (hard-coded in crashsender.exe). TCP accepted, HEAD answered with an empty reply.
  • http://bts.box.chomikuj.pl: Update infrastructure host (%1 = base.ini domain).
  • http://download.box.chomikuj.pl: Update infrastructure host (%1 = base.ini domain).
  • https://box.chomikuj.pl: The service also answers on HTTPS; the client never uses it.
